$comment: GOVERNED EGRESS MANIFEST — the complete list of modules permitted to contain an external
network primitive. Reviewed like code, asserted by scripts/check-egress-allowlist.mjs.
N7-A ships with ZERO approved modules. The manifest exists before the first primitive so that
the gate governing egress predates the thing it governs — otherwise its first exercise is the
very change that needs it, which is how a control becomes a formality.
Adding an entry is an owner-reviewed act. `expectedCount` must be updated in the same change,
so a widening is two lines in the diff rather than one, and it cannot be done by accident.
- entries are exact repo-relative file paths. No globs, no directory prefixes.
- every entry must resolve to a file that exists.
- an entry that contains NO egress primitive is STALE and fails. A standing permission
nobody is using will eventually be inherited by whatever moves into that path.
- a primitive outside this list fails, named by file and line.
This manifest does NOT grant permission to reach any particular address. Where an approved
module may connect is governed separately by the SSRF control set in N7_THREAT_MODEL.md §5.
